requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
The marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.authoring.invocation`, and each assertion enforces the expected outcome.

- **Subject kinds and existence.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `author` on both a requirement and a named example. It checks that each produces the matching `requirement` or `example` record.
  - `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` checks that an absent subject fails with a diagnostic naming it. It also checks that conflicting targets (a subject with `--all`, and `--all` with `--stdout`) exit with code 2, including through the `author-evidence` alias. The existing evidence is left unchanged.
- **Completion report.**
  - `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` checks that stdout starts with `{SUBJECT}: ollama / {MODEL}`. It also checks for an `Evidence:` line whose path resolves to `evidence/{SUBJECT}.json`, and a `Usage:` line.
  - The initial-prompt test checks the usage path is an existing file and the evidence path is the project's evidence file.
  - Together these cover subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage-record path.
- **Stdout mode.**
  - `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` checks that stdout parses entirely as a JSON record ending in a newline.
  - It checks that stderr carries `{SUBJECT}: ollama / {MODEL}`, `Evidence: stdout`, and a `Usage:` path.
  - It also checks that no evidence file is written or changed, across true, false and FIXME determinations, with and without existing evidence, and with and without `-v`.
  - The `--verbose` case runs with `--stdout` on the `author-evidence` alias.
- **Flags.**
  - `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` covers `--config <name>`. It checks that the alternate profile's model, key and backend are used, with `--force`.
  - `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers both `-v` and `--verbose`.
  - `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` covers `--missing`, `--force` and their mutual exclusion. It also covers `--stdout` rejecting `--missing` and implying `--force`, since a model call occurs on an otherwise-current record.
- **Refresh behaviour.**
  - The same batch test covers the cited `requirements.authoring.refresh` for a single subject. Current records are kept with a skipped-as-current report and no model call. This holds even with a broken configuration file.
  - It also covers `--force` reassessment and repair of invalid evidence under `--missing`.
- **Alias.** `author-evidence` is exercised in the missing/skip case and in the stdout, FIXME and initial-prompt tests.
- **Diagnostics to stderr.** The success-path diagnostics and report are checked on stderr in the stdout test. The diagnostic tests in `tests/authoring_batch.rs` for denied and untracked inputs under `--stdout` also check stderr or an empty stdout. Those two tests are not among the supplied marked tests, and I did not rely on them for the verdict.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behaviour that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
